baseline.title: JO9 FX animated-baseline
baseline.diagnosticOverride: Original scale/opacity animation held for observation with 6-second repeated animation
baseline.observation: The additional inset legacy vertical and bottom UI frame appeared while slash/player effects were animated, matching the user symptom.

candidateHeld.title: JO9 FX static-candidate
candidateHeld.diagnosticOverride: Static effects initially forced visible for a sustained comparison
candidateHeld.observation: Slash and player red tint were visible without the extra legacy frame. Two original attack links rendered subsequent combat states without an extra frame.

candidateLive.diagnosticOverride: None on CSS or JS; the visual hold was removed and a different diagnostic filename was opened to force a fresh game load
candidateLive.firstHit: Original attack link clicked; slash visible with normal frame, then absent on a later capture with the frame unchanged
candidateLive.secondHit: Original attack link clicked again; slash visible with normal frame, then absent on a later capture with the frame unchanged

preservation.userGame: Read-only initial inspection; no save/load/attack/close input sent to that window
preservation.screenshots: Inspected from native tool output only; screenshot payloads were not saved or re-encoded

limits: The visual baseline deliberately extends the original CSS animation to make its transient paint defect observable.
The fixed-size version removes animated scaling/fading while keeping the original images and 600/500ms production lifetimes.
Two actual GUI attack re-renders are distinct from the failed synthetic QSP re-entry harness and from the DOM timer unit test.
This does not certify every monster, battle route, graphics configuration or unrelated global UI repaint issue.
